title: Senator Rick Scott donates Senate salary to BRACE for Hurricane Isaias recovery efforts

Senator Rick Scott donates Senate salary to BRACE for Hurricane Isaias recovery efforts
Senator Rick Scott announced a donation of his third-quarter Senate salary to support Hurricane Isaias recovery through BRACE in Northwest Florida on Oct. 21. The contribution aims at aiding ongoing relief efforts coordinated by local organizations recognized nationally for disaster response.
Senator Rick Scott and Mrs. Anne Scott announced on Oct. 21 the donation of his third-quarter U.S. Senate salary to the Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies (BRACE), aiming to support families in Florida's Panhandle recovering from Hurricane Isaias. Since taking office in 2019, Scott has donated his Senate salary.
Scott said, “Anne and I are proud to partner with BRACE to support Floridians who face the long road ahead to recover from Hurricane Isaias. Floridians are tough. We come together when our neighbors need us the most, just as BRACE did before, during, and now after this storm. Anne and I are grateful to every Floridian who’s stepped up in a big way to help, and to BRACE for its commitment to coordinating long-term recovery efforts for Florida families. Our best days are always ahead, and we will get through this together.”
Dr. Nick Jackson, Chief Executive Officer of BRACE, said, “We are deeply honored and grateful that Senator Rick Scott has chosen BRACE as the recipient of his quarterly salary donation. In the wake of Hurricane Isaias, thousands of our neighbors across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties are facing tremendous challenges as they begin the long road to recovery. This generous contribution is more than a financial gift; it is a meaningful investment in the recovery and resilience of our communities. As BRACE continues coordinating volunteers, donations, and long-term recovery efforts across both counties, partnerships like this remind us that we are not facing these challenges alone. On behalf of BRACE and the communities we serve, I want to personally thank Senator Scott for his generosity, leadership, and commitment to helping Northwest Florida recover and rebuild.”
BRACE was established by member organizations of the Escambia Long-Term Recovery Committee in 2006 following lessons learned from Hurricane Ivan. The organization serves as Long-Term Recovery Group coordinator for Santa Rosa County with an anti-poverty focus aimed at supporting low-income residents affected by disasters.
BRACE acts as Citizen Corps Council and Community Emergency Response Team Coordinator for Escambia County, City of Pensacola, and Town of Century through volunteer engagement; it also coordinates Emergency Support Function 15 (Volunteers & Donations) under agreement with local emergency management agencies.
Since its founding in 2006, FEMA has recognized BRACE more frequently than any other locally-based coalition nationwide through its Individual and Community Preparedness Awards program—including receiving FEMA’s John D. Solomon Preparedness Award.
Scott champions fiscal responsibility along with policies supporting families; he served on active duty in the U.S. Navy after high school; earned degrees from University of Missouri-Kansas City (business) and Southern Methodist University (law); won election representing Florida in the U.S. Senate; serves on several key committees including Armed Services; raised two daughters with wife Anne—his high school sweetheart—all according to, the official website.
